questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that the destination was close so I could visit again (by train)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I came later than the arrival days, so not the easiest, but I still got all the information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a bag with information papers. Besides this, I had received information on email

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Mostly because I arrived late

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really easy through "myhousing"

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Uppsala there was no possibility to live on campus, but living off campus was great

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in Flogsta. It was great as many students live there. But if I had stayed more than a semester, I would choose another accommodation

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Apply for preapproval at home university, then send the preapproval and motivation to why I wanted the courses to the host institution. Quite circumstantial, but easy enough

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was descriptive information about how and when I was to do the different stages

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wanted to register for courses in Swedish, but I couldn't do that. But I got the courses i wanted in english.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just start as soon as possible so it won't become a stress factor

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied, but I think Uppsala University is better suited for following a program, rather than a handful of random courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses was a mix of BA and MA students

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As I took courses in CEMUS, the teachers were master/ph.d. students so it was a bit different than UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Critical Perspectives on Sustainable Development in Sweden
Global Challenges and Sustainable Futures
Environmental Ethnography 
Sustainable Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course Critical Perspectives on Sustainable Development in Sweden, as it is a great way to learn about Sweden while being critical

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was unexpected that i had to buy new wheels for my bike

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more or less as i expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The nations in Uppsala are a great both to be social, athletic, musical etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to join the nations and be a part of that part of Uppsala

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going skiing in the winter months (Järvsö is a good spot close to Uppsala) and also using the nature and hiking routes around Uppsala

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy as danish and swedish culture are quite similar

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that many actually :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the Fika culture in Sweden and also the language

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the three most important things would be to practice some Swedish before coming, to make use of Stockholm being so close and to enjoy the nation life, that is very different from UCPH.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe to join a program if it is possible instead of taking random courses

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding was definitely all the amazing people i met. Both other international students and Swedish people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was for me to live in a dorm room with many other people, as I hadn't done that before

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
